input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: There is no automatic-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. Maintenance runs for a "renewable one-year term" (p0065), i.e. renewal for a further 12 months requires the parties to agree and Sparkling to elect to pay the renewal maintenance fees; the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117), and Sparkling may in any event exit on ninety (90) days' notice at any time (p0118). That matches the preferred position (renewal by mutual agreement, 12-month periods, no evergreen lock-in and no non-renewal notice window to compute), and it is more favourable to us than the fallback. The only preferred sub-element absent is an express cap on renewal-fee uplift (lesser of CPI and 3%) — the Fee Schedule contains no escalation language at all, so there is no unilateral uplift right for Garman to exercise; we note this rather than flagging it, and would seek a CPI/3% cap on renewal maintenance fees if the Fee Schedule is reopened.
